tagline: Premium coffee and tea for consumers worldwide
hero_kpi_rationale: Core indicator of profitability and cost control for a consumer staples company.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: The portion of revenue that remains after paying direct production costs.
kpis.description: A stable and high gross margin indicates strong production cost management and perceived brand value.
kpis.signal: High gross margin, indicating strong cost control and brand power.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: The percentage of revenue that remains after all operating expenses.
kpis.description: Operating margin is improving due to efficiency gains and strict expense management.

kpis.name: R&D Investment (% of revenue)
kpis.explanation: What the company spends on innovation relative to its revenue.
kpis.description: R&D spending is limited, as innovation focuses on flavors, packaging, or sustainability, not technology.
kpis.signal: Very low R&D, typical for consumer staples, not pure tech.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Money invested annually in factories, machinery, and equipment.
kpis.description: Capital expenditures support the modernization of production sites and the sustainable transition.
kpis.signal: Moderate Capex, consistent with an organic growth model.

kpis.name: Total Headcount (in thousands)
kpis.explanation: Total number of people employed by the company.
kpis.description: Headcount is slightly decreasing, indicating cost optimization in an inflationary environment.
kpis.signal: Slight headcount reduction, likely aimed at improving productivity.

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last six fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of 0.36 EUR in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of 0.354 Bn EUR in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last four fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Portion of net income distributed as dividends: 44.5% in the latest year.

risks.title: Ongoing presence in Russia: major reputational risk
risks.score_rationale: Highlighted as a central theme throughout the document (central positioning), with highly intense language ('sponsors of war', 'condoning the war', 'legitimacy to the regime'). Trend worsening since 2022. Critical reputational category for a consumer staples company dependent on brand trust.

risks.title: Risk of expropriation of industrial assets in Russia
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly cited in the document as a reason invoked by JDE Peet's for staying (point 9), with references to Danone and Carlsberg cases. Factual language but real, documented risk. Trend increasing since partial nationalizations in 2022-2023.

risks.title: Damage to production infrastructure in Ukraine
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned (point 5): the Trostyanets plant (Ukraine) was damaged by combat. Direct operational risk to production capacity. Trend stable/worsening depending on conflict evolution.

risks.title: Risk of secondary sanctions and blacklisting
risks.score_rationale: Document explicitly cites the risk of being listed on the NACP 'International Sponsors of War' list and inclusion in World-Check (used globally by banks and insurers). Precise regulatory language. Trend increasing with the announced expansion of the NACP list.

risks.title: Russia rebranding strategy perceived as circumventing moral sanctions
risks.score_rationale: Point 8 of the document: replacement of Jacobs with Monarch with nearly identical packaging (green/gold, same fonts, same factory). The CEO himself describes the move as 'not risk-free'. Risk of bad faith perception by Western regulators and consumers.

risks.title: Exposure to human rights due diligence obligations
risks.score_rationale: Document explicitly references UNGPs, OECD Guidelines, UN Global Compact (of which JDE Peet's is a signatory). Legal precedents cited (Lafarge convicted for complicity in Syria). Trend increasing with tightening European legislation (CSDDD).

risks.title: HR risk: forced mobilization of Russian employees by the state
risks.score_rationale: Point 4 of the document: new Russian legislation requiring companies to assist in military call-ups and mobilization. Direct operational risk for ~900 employees in Russia. Trend increasing since the partial mobilization of September 2022.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence in the provided documents. The company does not position AI as a strategic lever.
evidence: No reference to AI in 10-K/20-F excerpts
Absence of projects related to automation, machine learning, or predictive analytics
Focus on traditional operations and ESG risks related to Russia
